### Knowing When to Eat
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/knowing-when-to-eat
Passage: 1 Corinthians 8:7-10
Points:
- Food itself is morally neutral and does not alter a believer's standing before God.
- Stronger believers in Corinth wrongly pressured others to join pagan feast meals.
- Believers from idolatrous backgrounds suffered wounded consciences when led into compromising situations.
- Noble intentions are insufficient when actions are disconnected from love and scriptural wisdom.
- Exercising Christian liberty must never become a stumbling block that harms another believer.

### So That No One May Stumble
Author: Michael A. Youssef, Ph.D.
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/leading-the-way/leading-the-way-devotional-for-august-12-2026.html
Passage: 1 Corinthians 8:9
Points:
- Christian freedom must always be tempered by genuine love for others in the church.
- Possessing sound doctrine means little if it is not matched by mature compassion.
- Believers are at varying stages of maturity and do not share identical understanding.
- Wounding a fellow believer's conscience through careless behavior is a sin against Christ.
- True spiritual maturity willingly lays aside personal rights and preferences for others' spiritual benefit.

### Liberty, Knowledge and Love
Author: Grace to You
Site: Grace to You
URL: https://www.gty.org/blogs/B140926/liberty-knowledge-and-love
Passage: 1 Corinthians 8:1
Points:
- Scripture grants freedom in non-essential areas, but that liberty requires careful discernment.
- Knowledge by itself tends to puff up, while love actively builds others up.
- Even when an action is permissible, self-interest should never outweigh a sibling's spiritual health.
- Causing a weaker Christian to stumble into sin is a serious spiritual offense.
- Believers are called to restrain their rights sacrificially for the spiritual growth of their community.
